override.reason: Approved past a block verdict from design review round 2 (3 HIGH, 1 MED, 1 could-not-verify; round 1's 5 HIGH and 3 MED were fixed in the revised LLD). The five open findings (user-facing claim and release commands, a second whoAmI call, guarding the daemon workflow driver, contested-claim wording, BUILD approval target mapping) are build-level details that do not change the chosen design; they are recorded as binding build requirements in docs/plans/team-workflow.md ("s5 LLD approval"). The add-only addAssignee amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-12 is a pending build prerequisite with s1.

summary.prose: Before a developer changes a stage (authors a step, builds, approves locally, applies a review finding, or opens a signoff request), the daemon asks one gate who holds the stage's tracker issue. The holder is the issue's assignee, read live. Only a stage nobody holds can be claimed, a claim never removes another assignee, and a stage someone else holds is refused naming them. Holders and administrators release a stage; nobody can take it over, and analyze and review are never blocked. GitHub cannot assign atomically, so two simultaneous claims are detected and reported, not prevented.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-side team gate over a synchronous, capability-declaring tracker port (alternative a1). The port (sc1) is the only way the workflow library talks to a tracker; GitHub is its first adapter, made by extracting the existing GitHub code (src/workflow/tracker, the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts, and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts) behind it. sc1 is the one tracker abstraction: the unbuilt tracker-tool design (LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1) is not built as a second abstraction and is superseded or amended by s1's LLD. The policy (sc2) is read from the remote default branch and says which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced, the claim units and the administrators. The artifact's tracker record keeps every existing meta.tracker field exactly as it is and gains additive per-unit data, plus an optional meta.revision (sc3). The team gate (sc4) takes a guarded action and returns an outcome. Signoff is a separate record (sc5) that never changes meta.review or approvedAt. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and the issue-status read it needs, are deferred with the later-tracker work to a define extend and are not part of this HLD.

ownedContracts.name: Team gate, claim state, gate outcome, refusal error and completion hook
ownedContracts.purpose: The single gate for guarded actions in the daemon-owned workflow library, the claim state read live from the tracker, the outcome type, the typed refusal error that leaves approval, the review-fix decision that both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) consult, and a completion hook that s5 ships unregistered and s7 registers. The gate derives the acting user itself through the port, so no caller signature changes. Owned by s5; s4 supplies issue creation which the gate calls for the no-issue outcome.

consumedContracts.name: TrackerPort and PortResult
consumedContracts.purpose: The only way the workflow library talks to a tracker. Declares capabilities, is checked against the capabilities the policy needs when loaded, returns structured results with a distinct error for a missing tool or sign-in, and can say who the signed-in user is so the gate knows who is acting. An issue reference is the existing owner/repo#N string. Owned by s1 because s1 is a root and every consumer depends on it.

consumedContracts.name: TeamPolicy
consumedContracts.purpose: The central rules read from the remote default branch: team mode, signoff stages, claim enforcement, claim units, administrators, and the grandfathering anchor. Owned by s2.

consumedContracts.name: Per-unit tracker record and revision
consumedContracts.purpose: Adds data next to the artifact's existing meta.tracker without changing any existing field: a per-stage-unit issue map in a new key, and an optional meta.revision (default 0 when absent), minted on content writes and not on meta-only writes. A review that applies auto-fixes, whether through verdicts.ts or run-artifact.ts, is a content write; a report-only review is meta-only. Owned by s4, which also owns the inventory of artifact write paths and the shared issue-creation code.

boundary.internal: The team gate and its call sites (daemon step entry points and approveArtifactByJsonPath), the acting-user read through the port, claim and release commands, live assignee reads, the guarded-action list (code-review and analyze are never guarded; review is never refused), the report-only review for a non-holder through the review-fix decision on both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts), the typed TeamGateRefusedError, its handling beside ReviewBlockedError in approveWorkflowTarget and its formatting in the terminal client's approve case in src/cli/command.ts, the no-issue outcome handling, administrator release, and the declaration of the completion hook, shipped unregistered.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The GitHub adapter built by extracting src/workflow/tracker (including the existing signed-in-user read, ghCurrentLogin, behind whoAmI), the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts behind the port; the gh command wrapper with its 10-second timeout; contract tests; detection of a missing tool or sign-in. The port receives the needed capabilities as an argument, so s1 does not read the policy. Reconciliation: the unbuilt tracker-tool design LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1 (docs/standalone/add-add-items-tracker-setting-have-E2026100638436e90/S001/LLD.md) is not built as a second abstraction; sc1 is the one tracker abstraction and s1's LLD supersedes or amends that LLD, once its conflicting approval status is settled. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and an issue-status read on the port, are deferred to the define extend.

Reading the policy file from the remote default branch ref, the cached last-fetched copy and the offline rule, finding the first default-branch commit that carried the policy file, the starter policy and the team setup command.

The repo-scoped kind of row in the shared settings catalog whose reads and writes go to the per-repo map in github.json read by resolveGithubConfig; its rendering in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal client; read-only display of policy values. Shares the single store with s1's target resolution.

Shared issue-creation code refactored out of autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan, find-by-label dedupe for Story and Task issues, forcing Task issues on in team mode, daemon-side triggering when a draft is first written, the terminal approve path kept as manual fallback, the inventory and classification of artifact write paths (including the two writeFileSync writers, and both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts as content writes when auto-fixes change the body), the single content-write helper and the revision minting, the bypass test that also detects raw writeFileSync on artifact paths, and the rule that an artifact without meta.revision reads as revision 0.
Parking a draft on a handoff branch, the issue note, resuming from committed files, and reconstructing in-flight workflow state from committed artifacts instead of the opaque token.

Opening the signoff request with the chosen artifacts, prerequisite checks for model review and local approval, registering the completion hook to produce the awaiting-signoff outcome, the on-demand completion check, automatic release of the claim on completion, recording sign-off together, grandfathering of artifacts approved before the policy anchor, and the separate display of signoff.
Revision of an open request: re-run of local approval, push to the same request, discarding an earlier completion, refusing non-holders.
Private implementation of s9: Keep tracker issues and status in step with the work without a manual step

nonFunctional.performance: Each guarded action makes at most two live reads through the port (the signed-in user and the assignee); every tracker command has a 10-second timeout, after which the action is refused with the reason. A repo without a policy makes no tracker call.
nonFunctional.security: Policy is read only from the remote default branch ref and is not locally overridable; enforcement lives in the daemon-owned workflow library (k1); no tracker secrets are stored by insrc, sign-in stays with the tracker's CLI; administrators come only from the policy.
nonFunctional.observability: Every gate outcome other than allowed is logged with unit, action and reason; port failures carry their kind (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected).
nonFunctional.durability: Claim, issue and signoff state live in the tracker and in committed artifact files; the in-memory step state stores (100 entries, 1 hour) are not relied on for handoff. Artifact writes stay atomic through the existing helper.

api.name: TeamGate
api.signature: (repo: string, unit: UnitRef, action: GuardedAction) => GateOutcome

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Absolute repo path; the policy and the tracker target are read for it

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The stage unit (Epic, Story or Task) the action changes

parameters.name: action
parameters.purpose: What the actor wants to do

returns.meaning: allowed (implicitClaim true when the gate just assigned the actor), held-by-other naming the holder, awaiting-signoff from the registered completion hook, no-issue (with allowFirstAuthor true only for the first author turn of a stage), or refused with a reason

errors.condition: Every failure (policy unreadable, tracker missing or signed out, several assignees, a timeout, a throwing hook) is returned as refused with the reason

preconditions: action is a guarded action; analyze and code review have no GuardedAction value and never reach the gate
postconditions: A repo with no policy, teamMode false or claimsEnforced false returns allowed with no tracker call
A non-allowed outcome is logged with unit, action and reason
After the tracker is loaded (loadTracker verifies the signed-in user once and the gate reuses it) the gate makes one live assignee read, plus the reads and writes of an implicit claim
Local issue resolution may reconcile the unit record on disk before a later tracker failure; it never writes content or approval state
For author and build the registered completion hook is consulted first, so a stage whose previous stage awaits signoff is refused

api.name: claim

returns.meaning: allowed when the actor now holds an unassigned unit (or already did); held-by-other when someone else does; refused when the claim is contested or a port step failed

postconditions: Only an unassigned unit is claimed
The claim adds the actor and never removes another assignee, then re-reads; more than one assignee afterwards is reported as contested
The tracker race between the read and the add is a documented limit (docs/plans/team-workflow.md, s5 claim atomicity)

api.name: release

returns.meaning: allowed when the assignees are cleared; refused for anyone but the holder or a policy administrator

postconditions: The assignee is cleared and others can claim
An administrator may release whoever the holder is, including a contested claim with several assignees
A release started by the completion hook does not consult the hook again

api.name: ReviewFixDecision

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit whose artifact is being reviewed

returns.meaning: apply-auto-fixes for the holder or when no gate applies; report-only for a non-holder or a failed read

errors.condition: A failed read yields report-only in team mode

preconditions: Consulted by both automatic review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) before they apply fixes
postconditions: A review is never refused; only its fix mode changes

api.name: RegisterCompletionHook

parameters.name: hook
parameters.purpose: Called by the gate for author and build on a next stage and for open-signoff, revise and release; s7 registers it

returns.meaning: The hook is stored; this Story registers none

postconditions: With no hook registered the gate behaves as if the hook returned continue
The hook's own release goes through the non-recursive internal path

api.name: approveArtifactByJsonPath
api.signature: (jsonPath: string, opts?: { readonly overrideReview?: string }) => ApprovalResult

errors.condition: In team mode the gate does not allow approve-local; thrown before any review check or stamp

postconditions: Signature unchanged; a repo with no policy behaves exactly as before

api.name: approveWorkflowTarget
api.signature: (req: WorkflowApproveRequest, opts?: { readonly enforce?: boolean }) => Promise<WorkflowApproveResult>

returns.meaning: Unchanged; a TeamGateRefusedError puts the artifact in skipped[] with the refusal reason, as ReviewBlockedError does

postconditions: Each target is authorized before ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion creates or merges its BUILD record, so a refused target is not changed
Other targets of a batch are still approved

api.name: resolveReviewFinding
api.signature: (artifactPath: string, jsonPath: string, findingId: string, action: ReviewAction, note?: string) => ResolveReviewResult

errors.condition: Action apply changes content, so a non-holder is refused before anything is written; accept, override and defer are meta-only and are not guarded

postconditions: Signature unchanged; the terminal resolve command shows the refusal

dataModelChanges.details: Tagged union returned by the gate: allowed {implicitClaim}, held-by-other {holder, offerPark}, awaiting-signoff {request}, no-issue {allowFirstAuthor, creationFailure?}, refused {reason}. Never persisted.
{ unit, holder: string | null, readAt }: the assignee read live for one call. In memory only; the tracker is the source of truth, so nothing about the claim is stored in artifacts.
Error subclass carrying the non-allowed outcome and its reason; thrown by approveArtifactByJsonPath, resolveReviewFinding (apply) and the daemon step entry points, handled beside ReviewBlockedError.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Owns GuardedAction, GateOutcome, ClaimState, TeamGate, TeamGateRefusedError, ReviewFixDecision, CompletionHook and RegisterCompletionHook as sketched; the hook is declared and left unregistered for s7, and is consulted for author and build on a next stage as well as for open-signoff, revise and release.

Uses loadTracker with the claim capability, whoAmI, readAssignee and setAssignee (release only). A claim needs the add-only addAssignee, proposed to s1 as amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-12 and pending; until it is agreed the build uses a fake port that implements it.
Reads teamMode, claimsEnforced and administrators through policyReader; a team repo whose policy cannot be read refuses a guarded action, a repo that never had a policy reads as none.
Finds the unit's issue with resolveUnitIssueLocal (which may reconcile the unit record) and creates a missing one with ensureUnitIssue for the no-issue outcome.

errorCases.scenario: The tracker cannot be reached, gh is missing, or the user is signed out when a guarded action is attempted in a team repo.
errorCases.detection: loadTracker, readAssignee or addAssignee returns a PortResult failure with kind missing-tool, missing-signin or unreachable.
errorCases.response: The gate returns refused with the port's reason and kind; the action does not run and nothing is written except possible metadata reconciliation done by local issue resolution before the tracker load.
errorCases.userImpact: The author is told the stage cannot be changed until the tracker is reachable, with the reason; analyze and review still work.

errorCases.scenario: The stage unit's issue has two or more assignees (a contested claim, or an issue assigned by hand).
errorCases.detection: readAssignee returns a rejected failure whose reason names the assignees (the GitHub adapter refuses a multi-assignee issue).
errorCases.response: The gate returns refused with that reason and never guesses a holder; an administrator's release clears every assignee, after which one developer claims again.
errorCases.userImpact: The author sees who is assigned and is told to ask an administrator to release.

errorCases.detection: readAssignee returns a login that differs from the signed-in login (compared case-insensitively).
errorCases.response: The gate returns held-by-other naming the holder; the entry point throws TeamGateRefusedError (daemon steps, approveArtifactByJsonPath, resolveReviewFinding apply) or maps it into skipped[] (approveWorkflowTarget). No time or inactivity is consulted, so a long-idle holder is still the holder.
errorCases.userImpact: The action is refused naming the holder; analyze and review still run (review in report-only mode).

errorCases.scenario: A non-holder who is not an administrator tries to release a stage.
errorCases.detection: release compares the signed-in login with the live assignee and with policy.administrators.
errorCases.response: release returns refused and does not call setAssignee.
errorCases.userImpact: The actor is told only the holder or an administrator may release.

errorCases.scenario: Two developers claim the same unassigned stage at the same moment.
errorCases.detection: Both read no assignee, both call addAssignee; the claim's re-read after the add shows more than one assignee, or the other's login.
errorCases.response: The claim returns refused as contested and removes nobody; the stage then reads as several assignees until an administrator releases it. GitHub offers no atomic assign-if-unassigned, so this is detected after the fact and documented as a known limit (docs/plans/team-workflow.md, s5 claim atomicity).
errorCases.userImpact: Both claimants are told the claim is contested and that an administrator must release; no work is lost.

errorCases.scenario: addAssignee or setAssignee fails or times out partway.
errorCases.detection: The port returns a PortResult failure (its own re-read does not match).
errorCases.response: claim and release return refused with the reason and say the resulting state is unknown; no retry runs inside the call.
errorCases.userImpact: The actor is told to read the claim again before acting.

errorCases.scenario: The stage unit has no issue and one cannot be found or created.
errorCases.detection: resolveUnitIssueLocal returns null and ensureUnitIssue returns a failure (for a Story, because its LLD does not exist yet).
errorCases.response: The gate returns no-issue with creationFailure. allowFirstAuthor is true only for the first author turn of a stage that has no artifact yet, and the entry point lets that one draft be written instead of throwing; every other action is refused. After the draft is written the draft hook creates the issue, and the implicit claim is taken by the gate on the next guarded turn.
errorCases.userImpact: The author can write the first draft; the stage cannot be claimed or changed further until its issue exists.

errorCases.scenario: The team policy cannot be read for a repo that is known to carry one.
errorCases.detection: policyReader returns ok:false (it reports a known team repo as unreadable, never as none).
errorCases.response: A guarded action is refused with the reason; a repo that never had a policy reads as none and is unaffected.
errorCases.userImpact: The author is told the policy cannot be read and how to refresh it.

errorCases.scenario: The review-fix decision cannot read the claim.
errorCases.detection: readAssignee or the tracker load fails inside ReviewFixDecision.
errorCases.response: It returns report-only: the review runs and lists findings but applies no auto-fix.
errorCases.userImpact: Findings are listed; the holder applies fixes.

errorCases.scenario: A registered completion hook throws, or calls release.
errorCases.detection: The gate wraps the hook call in try/catch, and the hook's release goes through an internal path that does not consult the hook.
errorCases.response: A throw returns refused with the hook's message and the action does not run; a release from the hook cannot recurse.
errorCases.userImpact: The author sees the hook's error; the stage is not changed.

errorCases.scenario: An approval target is refused but its BUILD record does not exist yet.
errorCases.detection: approveWorkflowTarget authorizes each target before it calls ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion.
errorCases.response: The target goes to skipped[] with the refusal reason and no BUILD record is created or merged for it.
errorCases.userImpact: A refused approval leaves the repo unchanged.

edgeCases.input: A repo with no policy file, teamMode false, or claimsEnforced false.
edgeCases.expected: allowed with implicitClaim false and no tracker call; behaviour is exactly as before this Story.

edgeCases.input: The actor already holds the stage and acts again.
edgeCases.expected: allowed with implicitClaim false; no addAssignee call.

edgeCases.input: Nobody holds the stage and the actor authors or builds.
edgeCases.expected: allowed with implicitClaim true; the gate adds the actor through addAssignee before returning, and a failed or contested add refuses the action.

edgeCases.input: Nobody holds the stage and the actor approves locally or applies a review finding.
edgeCases.expected: allowed with implicitClaim false and no assignment: approving or applying does not take a claim.

edgeCases.input: A developer was assigned directly in the tracker and acts without claiming.
edgeCases.expected: They are the holder because the assignee is read live; allowed with implicitClaim false.

edgeCases.input: Analyze or code review on a stage someone else holds.
edgeCases.expected: Never reaches the gate; works as before.

edgeCases.input: Automatic review or the accept, override and defer resolutions of a finding on a stage someone else holds.
edgeCases.expected: They run: the automatic review is report-only through ReviewFixDecision, and accept, override and defer are meta-only and unguarded.

edgeCases.input: Author or build on the next stage while the previous stage's signoff is open or not yet complete.
edgeCases.expected: The gate consults the registered completion hook, which may return awaiting-signoff; with no hook registered the gate continues.

edgeCases.input: A login differs only in case from the signed-in login.
approveWorkflowTarget is given a batch where one artifact is held by someone else.
edgeCases.expected: That artifact is in skipped[] with the refusal reason and no BUILD record is created for it; the others are approved.

alternativesConsidered.name: One gate function, called explicitly at each guarded entry point, with an inventory test
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A single teamGate(repo, unit, action) in the workflow library; every entry point that changes a stage calls it first; a test lists the guarded entry points so a new one cannot forget.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add src/workflow/team/gate.ts exporting teamGate, claim, release, reviewFixDecision, registerCompletionHook and TeamGateRefusedError. teamGate reads the policy and returns allowed with no tracker call when there is no policy, teamMode is false, claimsEnforced is false, or the action is not guarded. Otherwise it loads the tracker with the claim capability, reuses the identity that load verified, reads the assignee live, and decides: the assignee is the holder; an unassigned stage lets the actor proceed and, for author and build, takes an implicit claim through the add-only addAssignee (never removing anyone); another holder gives held-by-other; several assignees give refused (never a guessed holder). The first author turn of a stage whose issue cannot be created yet is the one explicit exception: the gate returns no-issue with allowFirstAuthor true, the entry point lets that draft be written, and the draft hook then creates the issue and the implicit claim is taken by the gate on the next guarded turn. The guarded entry points are the workflow-step phases, the build-step phases, approveArtifactByJsonPath, approveWorkflowTarget (authorized before ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion), and the content-changing review resolution (resolveReviewFinding with action apply, reached from the terminal resolve command); automatic review fixes consult reviewFixDecision. For author and build on a next stage the gate also consults the registered completion hook, and the hook's own release call goes through a non-recursive internal release that skips the hook. claim and release are commands: claim only takes an unassigned stage; release clears the assignee for the holder or a policy administrator.
pros: Smallest change that covers every path the review found, with the call sites the HLD names
The refusal sits beside ReviewBlockedError and reuses its handling
An inventory test makes a forgotten entry point a test failure, not a silent hole
cons: About ten call sites each derive their own UnitRef
Needs the add-only addAssignee port operation from s1 (amendment pending) for a claim that never removes anyone

alternativesConsidered.name: Wrap the daemon step handlers in a gate middleware
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One wrapper around the workflow-step, build-step and review-step handlers derives the unit and action from the request and applies the gate before the handler runs.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A higher-order guardHandler(handler, describe) maps a request to { unit, action } or undefined for unguarded requests, and the daemon registers the handlers through it. A handler registered later through the wrapper is covered
cons: The unit must be derived from the request before the handler has parsed it: later phases carry only the opaque state token, so the wrapper duplicates parsing or reads the state store
Approval and finding resolution run outside the daemon handlers, so two mechanisms exist
A phase that should stay unguarded needs a special case
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Two mechanisms are needed and the unit must be derived from the opaque state token before the handler parses it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Enforce in the artifact writer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: writeArtifact (kind content) asks the gate before it writes, so any content change by a non-holder is refused wherever it comes from.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Pass an optional action into writeArtifact and consult teamGate for kind content writes, so every path through the single writer s4 built is covered, and let the gate derive the unit from the artifact path.
pros: Cannot be bypassed by a new caller that writes content
Reuses the s4 inventory as the coverage proof
cons: Couples the storage layer to the tracker and policy
Refuses at write time, after the draft has been generated, so the author loses work; the HLD wants the refusal before the action
